items.check: No face, avatar or synthetic human in any frame
items.note: Twenty-eight frames, no person anywhere. The film is charts and kinetic type only.

items.check: Texture is never the subject being explained
items.note: No Higgsfield or world shot appears at all; the paper room carries the whole film.

items.check: Every on-screen number traces to a real run; demo data is labelled
items.note: Every figure matches facts.json from the Tarnhollow demo run, and the demo chip sits bottom left on every frame that carries a figure. See item 15 for the wording of one label.

items.check: Charts are Manim scenes driven by engine output
items.note: The cash cone and the ninety-day stair are the engine's own paths; axis maxima are the run's, not round numbers.

items.check: Every chart builds progressively and carries an annotation
items.note: events.json records sixteen landings across the nine segments: axes, then paths, then the median and percentile annotations.

items.check: Room tone, data ticks, transition SFX and a ducking bed are present
items.note: media/mix.json: room tone at -48 dB, bed at -32 dB ducking to -20 dB, seven ticks, two whooshes, -16 LUFS, measured at -16.5.
voice is 'library', the ElevenLabs library voice the founder chose in content/assets/voice.json on 2026-10-04, with its disclosure line ready for the description.

items.check: No shot holds longer than six seconds
items.note: The master is nine shots over 275 s: 18.2, 29.8, 37.6, 1.1, 50.2, 1.1, 55.2, 46.8 and 35.2 seconds. scdet finds zero cuts in the whole film. The production bible asks for a cut every two to four seconds and nothing over about six. Two kinetic cards hold a single unchanged picture while the narration runs for most of a minute: 'Here's the model most of us run on.' across f-003 to f-005, and 'A short list, and you can do all of it this week.' across f-020 to f-024. events.json shows the same gaps from the other side: nothing lands on screen between 19.2 s and 86.7 s, or between 153.3 s and 194.2 s. qa.py's holds_over_6s read 0 because freezedetect sees the subtitles changing underneath a still picture, so the program check cannot catch this one.

items.check: Subtitles are burned in, legible, light and never boxed
items.note: The style is right, unboxed Inter in ink, but on every chart segment the block sits on the chart's own x-axis row and overwrites it. f-006, f-010, f-011 and f-014 lose the d182 and d273 tick labels under the words; f-015 and f-017 to f-019 run the second line straight through the baseline and its ticks. The subtitle needs to clear the axis, either by lifting the block above the plot's bottom margin on chart shots or by raising the plot.
Not applicable yet: V01 is the unit that writes the lock, and it is written after this step passes.

items.check: One blue element per frame, blue only on money and the leak
items.note: Blue appears on the cash paths, the money figures and the percentile callouts, and nowhere else. No red, no green, no gradient, glow or halo. Chapter cards are typographic.

items.check: At most three text blocks per frame
items.note: f-012, f-013 and f-014 carry the headline, two stacked stat cards, two chart annotations, the subtitle and the demo chip at once, and the elements collide: the blue '$65,320' callout is drawn on top of the '7%' annotation and the stat card beneath it, so f-013 and f-014 read '$9%5,320' and '3%5,320'. No figure on those frames is readable.

items.check: Charts carry direct labels, a demo label, no legend and no grid
items.note: The labels are direct and there is no legend or grid, but the stat rail's captions are clipped at two lines and stop mid-sentence: 'mean ending cash of the bottom tenth after' (f-012 to f-014) and 'mean trough of the top tenth over' (f-016 to f-019). Both lose the words that say over what period, which is the part that makes the figure mean anything. The rail also does not retire a figure when the narration moves on: f-009 still shows 'cash on hand today' while the chart is annotating percentiles.

items.check: Nothing on screen is empty or dead
items.note: f-025, at about 245 s, is a blank paper frame: no headline, no chart, no figure, only the subtitle and the demo chip. The segment the narration calls 'running a year of a twenty-four-product catalog' has nothing on it.

items.check: Nothing on a client surface implies a client that does not exist
items.note: The stat card in f-007 to f-009 reads 'cash on hand today (client-stated)', from the label in facts.json. Hubricon has no clients, and the demo chip beside it says the figures are a demo fixture, so the word 'client' on screen is the one thing in the film that is not true. The label belongs in the demo's own vocabulary: 'stated by the seller in the demo fixture', or simply 'cash on hand today'. The same wording sits on monthly_fixed_costs.

notes: The look is right and the honesty furniture is in place: paper ground, Inter, one blue and only on money, the demo chip on every frame that carries a figure, every number out of the engine's own run, and the sound layered as the bible asks. What fails is the cut and the layout. The film is nine very long shots with no cuts at all, so two kinetic cards sit unchanged for the better part of a minute each; the subtitle block lands on the chart's x-axis and takes the tick labels with it; the right-hand stat rail clips its captions mid-sentence, keeps stale figures and collides with the chart's own annotations until the figures are unreadable; one segment is blank. The fixes are upstream of assemble, in the scene renderer and the subtitle placement, not in the mix. The 'client-stated' label is the one honesty item and it is a one-line change in the facts labels.
